{{short description|Italian physicist}}
'''Luisa Ottolini''' (born July 10, 1954, in  [[Tortona]], [[province of Alessandria]], [[Italy]]) is an Italian [[physicist]].

==Biography==
In 1978, Luisa Ottolini graduated in [[Physics]] at the [[University of Pavia]]. From 1982 to 1986, she was the Head of the Structuristic Section at the Istituto Sperimentale dei Metalli Leggeri (I.S.M.L.) in [[Novara]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cpseditrice.it/cpo/settimana04/ottolini.htm|title=CNR - Comitato per le Pari OportunitÃ - ricercatrici d'eccelenza - Luisa Ottolini|first=Niklas Andersson, Lorena Nurzia - Conosci per|last=scegliere|website=www.cpseditrice.it}}</ref> In 1987, she activated the Strategic Project of the National Research Council of Italy (CNR) ''An Ion Microprobe for Advanced Researches in the Earth Sciences'' with the installation at the “Centro di Studio per la Cristallografia Strutturale” in Pavia of the first, and so far, the only one National Laboratory of [[Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry]] ([[Secondary ion mass spectrometry|SIMS]]) in the Earth Sciences. Since that time she has been the Head of the SIMS Lab. Starting from 1989, she activated the National SIMS service for University and CNR Institutions offering the Earth Science Committee (05), following more than 90 research projects.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cnr.it/sitocnr/IlCNR/Chisiamo/Storia/CNRalfemminile/Ottolini.html|title=CNR-->Storia del CNR al femminile|website=www.cnr.it}}</ref> In 2002-2005 she coordinated a research Unit in Pavia, sponsored by the European Framework Project EUROMELT<ref>[ftp://ftp.cordis.europa.eu/pub/improving/docs/rtn_project_summaries_2nd_call.pdf EUROMELT, January 2013]{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> (European Community’s Human Potential Programme, contract HPRN-CT-2002-00211). Between December 2005 and September 2017 she was the Head of CNR-Institute of Geosciences and Geo-resources (IGG)-Section of Pavia.

She has co-authored more than 150 international ISI publications, of which 5 in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'';<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Schiano|first1=Pierre|last2=Clocchiatti|first2=Roberto|last3=Ottolini|first3=Luisa|last4=Busà|first4=Tiziana|title=Transition of Mount Etna lavas from a mantle-plume to an island-arc magmatic source|journal=Nature|volume=412|issue=6850|pages=900–904|doi=10.1038/35091056|pmid=11528476|year=2001|bibcode=2001Natur.412..900S|s2cid=4425759}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Complementary Ti and Zr anomalies in orthopyroxene and clinopyroxene from mantle peridotites|first1=Elisabetta|last1=Rampone|first2=Piero|last2=Bottazzi|first3=Luisa|last3=Ottolini|journal=Nature|volume=354|issue=6354|pages=518|doi=10.1038/354518a0|bibcode=1991Natur.354..518R|year=1991|s2cid=4335564}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ligi|first1=Marco|last2=Bonatti|first2=Enrico|last3=Cipriani|first3=Anna|last4=Ottolini|first4=Luisa|title=Water-rich basalts at mid-ocean-ridge cold spots|journal=Nature|volume=434|issue=7029|pages=66–69|doi=10.1038/nature03264|pmid=15744299|bibcode=2005Natur.434...66L|year=2005|s2cid=254959|url=https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8PK0RWV/download|hdl=11380/703800|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bonatti|first1=Enrico|last2=Ligi|first2=Marco|last3=Brunelli|first3=Daniele|last4=Cipriani|first4=Anna|last5=Fabretti|first5=Paola|last6=Ferrante|first6=Valentina|last7=Gasperini|first7=Luca|last8=Ottolini|first8=Luisa|title=Mantle thermal pulses below the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and temporal variations in the formation of oceanic lithosphere|journal=Nature|volume=423|issue=6939|pages=499–505|doi=10.1038/nature01594|pmid=12774114|bibcode=2003Natur.423..499B|year=2003|s2cid=4416441|url=https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8TB1HN1/download|hdl=11380/583637|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Spengler|first1=Dirk|last2=Roermund|first2=Herman L. ==Main scientific interests==

Her research activities mainly concerned the use of SIMS for the quantitative measurement of low-concentration constituents, of light ([[Lithium]], [[Beryllium]] and [[Boron]]) and volatile elements ([[Hydrogen]], [[Fluorine]], [[Chlorine]], [[Carbon]]) in geological samples, with particular reference to the investigation of the physical/chemical processes underlying the production of secondary ions, aiming at overcoming the limitations of the technique (interferences and non-linear effects, “matrix effects”); the development, set up and optimization of SIMS procedures for trace elements,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ottolini |first=Luisa |last2=Bottazzi |first2=Piero |last3=Vannucci |first3=Riccardo |last4=Oddone |first4=Massimo |date=1992-04-01 |title=AN ION PROBE CONTRIBUTION ==Awards and honors==
* 2004 - Awards from CNR in the celebration of the 80th anniversary of the foundation of CNR, as one of the 12 CNR female researchers who contributed to the development of the scientific progress of [[Italy]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CNR-->Storia del CNR al femminile |url=http://www.cnr.it:80/sitocnr/IlCNR/Chisiamo/Storia/CNRalfemminile/Ottolini.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170331172650/http://www.cnr.it:80/sitocnr/IlCNR/Chisiamo/Storia/CNRalfemminile/Ottolini.html |archive-date=2017-03-31 |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=www.cnr.it}}</ref>
* 2004 - The name of [[Ferri-ottoliniite]] to a new [[amphibole]] end-member (IMA-CNMMN 2001-67A) to acknowledge the “fundamental contribution of L. Ottolini to the advancement of ion-probe analysis of [[minerals]], with particular  reference to [[light elements]]”.<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Mineralogist {{!}} GeoScienceWorld |url=https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/ammin |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=pubs.geoscienceworld.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://webmineral.com/data/Ferri-ottoliniite.shtml|title=Ferri-ottoliniite Mineral Data|first=Dave|last=Barthelmy|website=webmineral.com}}</ref>
* 2006 - Inclusion of L. Ottolini in  [[Who’s Who in the World]] (23rd Edition by Marquis, Who’s Who, Philadelphia, PA, USA) and in ''Who's Who in Science and Engineering''.
* Since 2013 - Partner of the [[University of Liège]].
